item.title: Is it worse to eat junk food early in the day?
item.description: The body can process food more efficiently in the morning but blood sugar spikes and hunger pangs can quickly crop up after an unhealthy meal.
item.content:encoded:
Many of us have grown up with the mantra that breakfast is the most important meal of the day.

But whether it’s snatching an extra half hour of sleep, or focusing on getting the kids out of the house, there are various reasons why assembling a healthy breakfast might slip down your list of priorities – especially on a weekday.

So, is it worse to eat unhealthy foods first thing, compared to later in the day? And what about skipping breakfast altogether?

It’s not just about calories

You probably know eating foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fats – especially when they’re highly processed – puts you at greater risk of a range of serious health conditions. These include diabetes, heart disease and some cancers.

Poor diet can also affect our gut health, mental health and reproductive health.

Eating a diet high in vegetables and fruit, lean meat and alternatives, such as chicken and lentils, wholegrains, and reduced-fat dairy and alternatives (such as plant-based yoghurt) will improve your overall health and wellbeing, and reduce the risk of serious health conditions.

For breakfast, aim to include a source of good-quality protein, wholegrains, fruit and/or vegetables and healthy fats.

item.title: UP: Muslim driver dies four days after being assaulted by kanwariyas following road accident
item.description: A purported video of the incident has been shared widely on social media which shows Azeem Ali being attacked by a group in the presence of a police officer.
item.content:encoded:
A 24-year-old Muslim truck driver died of his injuries four days after he was assaulted by a group of kanwariyas in Hapur district in Uttar Pradesh, The Print reported on Friday.

The assault followed an argument after Azeem Ali’s truck collided with an auto-rickshaw hired by the kanwariyas in Garhmukhteshwar town on July 31. The collision allegedly injured the auto-rickshaw driver, Farman, who was standing near the vehicle. Ali was then allegedly pulled out of his truck and assaulted.

A purported video of the incident has been shared widely on social media which shows Ali being assaulted by a group of men in the presence of a police officer.

Ali was initially taken to hospital in Meerut and later shifted to Delhi as his condition worsened. He reportedly went into a coma and died at a Delhi hospital on Tuesday, The Print reported.

A first information report has been registered against seven persons, including four kanwariyas, in connection with Ali’s murder.

Five persons identified as Manish, Ankit, Lokesh, Shivam and Farman, along with two unidentified persons, have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita pertaining to murder, rioting and voluntarily causing hurt, The Print reported.

No arrests have been made so far.

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye sign defence pact amid conflict in West Asia
item.description: India said that it was ‘closely following’ the agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye on Friday signed a joint defence agreement on Friday, amid the conflict in West Asia.

India said that it was “closely following” the new defence pact.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, is aimed at “strengthening collective deterrence” and states that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be considered an attack against all.

It also seeks to enhance defence cooperation among the three countries and promote peace, security and stability in the region and beyond.

However, the agreement does not specify detailed military commitments or obligations that have been accepted, Reuters reported.

An unidentified Turkish official told the news agency that the pact was “purely defensive in nature” and was not directed against any particular country.

The official added that the pact was open to other regional countries and would not replace existing bilateral or multilateral defence arrangements.

The agreement was signed by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

It came against the backdrop of heightened tensions in West Asia amid conflict involving Iran, Israel and the United States.

The pact brings together three major Sunni Muslim-majority states: Saudi Arabia, the Gulf’s strongest economy, one of the world’s top oil exporters and home to Islam’s holiest sites, Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim-majority country and Türkiye, which has North Atlantic Treaty Organization’s second-largest military.

item.title: Nepal’s demolition drive leaves thousands homeless, violates human rights
item.description: The government and armed forces evicted mostly poor and marginalised residents of Kathmandu.
item.content:encoded:
The mass eviction of slums and informal settlements in Nepal’s capital Kathmandu and surrounding districts has displaced an estimated 15,000-20,000 people.

On April 25, the Nepal government began forcibly removing landless residents from the Kathmandu Valley, later extending the drive beyond the capital.

Nepal faces a staggering crisis: more than 3.5 million people are landless or homeless. A government commission invited applications for registration, and 1.2 million people – mostly poor, Dalit, and indigenous – have already registered in the hope of receiving land. Ironically, these communities have borne the brunt of evictions carried out without adequate notice, consultation, or alternative housing. The lack of support has eroded their trust in the state.

The ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party pledged to resolve landlessness within 1,000 days of office. Its 100-point action plan also promised relief to the landless. Yet, despite decades of settlement – some families have been living in Kathmandu’s slums for 60 years – the government demolished homes using the full force of the state. Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, Nepal Army, and the municipal police participated. Residents were harassed, threatened, and even detained before demolitions.

item.description: How did a drug meant to treat diabetes become India’s top-selling drug within months of its launch?
item.content:encoded:
We went undercover to investigate the booming market for Mounjaro, an injectable that apart from type-II diabetes, can also be prescribed by specialist doctors for severe and complicated obesity. Effective for weight loss, it is not meant for everyone and should not be used without medical advice.

But, as we found, the prescription-only drug is available on tap. From chemist shops and online sellers agreeing to sell Mounjaro without a prescription to unauthorised doctors prescribing the drug as part of beauty treatments in aesthetic salons, many are profiting from India’s obsession with weight-loss – at a steep cost to the health of users.

item.title: FCRA amendments India’s internal matter: Centre after US lawmaker calls bill ‘attack’ on Christians
item.description: Congressman Riley Moore had warned that the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act could hurt bilateral relations.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of External Affairs on Friday said that proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act were India’s “internal affairs”, three days after a United States Congressman raised concerns about the move.

Registration under the Act is mandatory for non-profit organisations to receive foreign funds. A key provision of the draft legislation allows the Union government to take control of a non-governmental organisation’s foreign funds and assets if its FCRA registration lapses or is cancelled.

On Tuesday, Riley Moore, a Republican representative from West Virginia, criticised the proposed amendments, claiming that the Indian Parliament was trying to take control of churches and religious charities.

“Christians have been in India since St Thomas the Apostle travelled to the Malabar Coast just decades after the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ,” Moore said on social media.

Despite this long history, India’s Parliament is considering amending the rules “to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities”, he alleged.

He said that the bill would be “a clear attack against Christians” and claimed the move could hurt relations between Washington and New Delhi.

The bill was introduced in Parliament in March during the Budget Session but has not been cleared by either of the Houses.

item.title: Jharkhand protests: Ink thrown at student leader Neha Bora allegedly for supporting Umar Khalid
item.description: The All India Students’ Association president alleged that the man shouted ‘Jai Shri Ram’ after the incident.
item.content:encoded:
Ink was thrown at student leader Neha Bora on Friday during a protest in Ranchi against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in Jharkhand. The police have detained the alleged attacker, PTI reported.

Bora is the president of the All India Students’ Association, the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist).

The man, who was detained by the police, said that he had targeted Bora because of her support for jailed activist Umar Khalid, PTI reported.

“I do not like Neha Bora because she supports Umar Khalid,” PTI quoted him as saying. “…They are all anti-nationals.”

Khalid has been in jail since September 2020 for his alleged involvement in the communal violence that broke out in North East Delhi in February 2020 between supporters of the contentious Citizenship Amendment Act and those opposing it. The violence had left 53 dead and hundreds injured. Most of those killed were Muslims.

item.title: Bengal: Two BJP workers named in CBI chargesheet for murder of CM Suvendu Adhikari’s aide
item.description: One of them arranged and financed the killing by hiring shooters from Uttar Pradesh, alleged the investigation agency.
item.content:encoded:
Two Bharatiya Janata Party workers were among the 11 persons named in a chargesheet filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation in connection with the murder of an aide to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, PTI quoted unidentified officials as saying on Thursday.

Chandranath Rath was shot dead near Kolkata on May 6, two days after the West Bengal Assembly election results were declared. Adhikari, who became the chief minister on May 9, was not with Rath at the time of the attack. The BJP leader has alleged that it was a “pre-planned murder”.

Since taking over the investigation into Rath’s murder on May 12, the CBI has arrested 11 persons.

The two BJP workers named by the investigation agency are brothers Sagar Sonkar and Sahib Sonkar, The Hindu reported. They were arrested on August 1.

Sagar Sonkar had worked with Rath and was one of the key conspirators in his murder, an unidentified official was quoted as claiming by the newspaper. He allegedly arranged and financed the killing by hiring shooters from Uttar Pradesh.

He worked for an MLA from a rival political party until 2020, before joining the BJP, PTI quoted the CBI as claiming.

A BJP leader filed a complaint against the Krishnanagar MP, alleging that her comment had hurt the sentiments of the Hindu community.

item.title: Audio clip allegedly linking Manipur violence to former CM is manipulated, Centre tells SC
item.description: The government urged the bench to dismiss the plea that demanded an independent investigation into the recording.
item.content:encoded:
The Union government on Friday claimed before the Supreme Court that the audio clip allegedly linking former Manipur Chief Minister N Biren Singh to the ethnic violence in the state was manipulated, Bar and Bench reported.

The court was hearing a petition filed by the Kuki Organization for Human Rights Trust, which has demanded an independent investigation into the audio clips purportedly featuring Singh’s voice.

The government’s submission came after the National Forensic Sciences University in Gujarat’s Gandhinagar placed on record a forensics report about the authenticity of the clip.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, representing the Union government, quoted an expert at the separate Central Forensic Science Laboratories as having stated that the full audio clip had 41 alterations, Bar and Bench reported.

The counsel urged the bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva to dismiss the petition.

However, the bench ordered that a copy of the National Forensic Sciences University’s report be provided to the petitioner and the government, saying that both sides will be given an opportunity to address its content, the legal news outlet reported.

item.description: Matin Patel has been named in the chargesheet for allegedly providing refuge to Nida Khan, the main accused person in the sexual harassment matter.
item.content:encoded:
The Maharashtra Police has arrested All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen corporator Matin Patel for not responding to summonses issued by a court in connection with a sexual harassment case at the Tata Consultancy Services in Nashik, The Indian Express reported.

Patel was held after the court issued a non-bailable warrant against him for skipping two summonses.

The corporator has been named in the chargesheet for allegedly providing refuge to Nida Khan, the main accused in the case, despite knowing that her anticipatory bail plea had been rejected.

While the police were searching for Khan in April and May, “it was revealed through confidential information and technical analysis” that Patel had provided her shelter to help her evade arrest, The Indian Express cited the chargesheet as having alleged.

Khan was arrested on May 7 from a bungalow in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar’s Naregaon area that was owned by Patel.

She was held more than 40 days after being named in a first information report for allegedly hurting religious sentiments.

item.description: Arun Matheswaran’s Tamil action thriller stars Lokesh Kanagaraj in his acting debut alongside Wamiqa Gabbi.
item.content:encoded:
Having made his share of action thrillers, Lokesh Kanagaraj now stars in one. Arun Matheswaran’s DC stars the curly-haired director as the ‘D’ in ‘DC’: Devadas.

Yup, the same one who ruined himself through obsessive love and alcohol in Sarat Chandra Chatterjee’s classic novel Devdas. In DC, made in Tamil and dubbed into Telugu and Hindi, the destruction is turned outward while the alcohol continues to be copiously imbibed.

If ashes could turn, they would.

Kanagaraj’s Devadas is the leading light of a gang of armed robbers. Their latest heist brings them in the crosshairs of the police officer Bhojraj (Krish Dayal), who is keenly following the advice given to him by his boss: “Be brutal.”

Devadas and his mates, including Kitty (Avinash Raghudevan), go on the run, cutting down whoever crosses their path. But a heart of gold throbs behind Devadas’s epilated chest, compelling him to behave like Robin Hood when required and fall for sad-faced women who are awaiting rescue.

Devadas doesn’t succeed with the club singer Parvathi (Sanjana AK) but fares better with the rose-clutching sex worker Chandra (Wamiqa Gabbi). item.description: BJP leader Vijay Baghel has alleged that the former chief minister held a roadshow a day before the election, violating the Representation of the People Act.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a petition by Chhattisgarh’s former Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel, seeking that a plea challenging his victory in the 2023 Assembly elections be rejected, Live Law reported.

Bhupesh Baghel can raise his objections during the trial before the Chhattisgarh High Court, said a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.

The Congress leader represents the Patan constituency in the Chhattisgarh Assembly.

His victory was challenged by his rival, the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Vijay Baghel, who alleged that Bhupesh Baghel conducted a roadshow a day before the election on November 17, 2023.

This violated Section 126 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which requires candidates not to campaign 48 hours before the polling, alleged the BJP leader.

Appearing for Bhupesh Bhaghel, advocate Kapil Sibal told the court on Friday that the allegation amounted to a violation of the Act and could not be treated as a “corrupt practice”, Live Law reported.

There was no basis to suggest that the alleged roadshow had influenced the election outcome, Sibal added. He pointed out that Bhupesh Baghel had won by a margin of nearly 20,000 votes while Vijay Baghel alleges that only around 200 persons attended the event.

item.description: The other posts that were restricted in the country were about a meat ban in Amritsar and a US case about an alleged plot to kill a Khalistani leader.
item.content:encoded:
Instagram has blocked four posts by Scroll on the social media platform since June, citing “legal requirements” under the Union government’s Information Technology Rules.

The platform informed Scroll through a message on its dashboard that access to the content had been restricted in India “through an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements” under the rules.

On August 6, a post about Scroll’s report on how most pellet gun victims in Kashmir have not received compensation even a decade after they were injured was blocked. A second post with a photo in which pellet injuries were not visible, published later in the day, was also restricted. Instagram did not provide a specific reason for the actions.

On July 5, a post relating to a Scroll article about how Kashmir’s turbulent history has, for several years, provided grist for Bollywood creators looking to generate xenophobic content, was initially restricted when it included a screenshot from teaser of the film Chauhaan, showing pellet injuries. The petition was filed for “cheap publicity”, said a bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe.

Unaccounted cash was allegedly recovered at Varma’s official residence in Delhi when emergency services responded to a fire there on March 14, 2025. He was a judge at the Delhi High Court at that time.

The judge said that he was in Bhopal when the cash was discovered and claimed that it did not belong to him or his family.

The Kargil War of 1999 was fought between India and Pakistan on snowy peaks and in thin air. The conflict, which gave India a decisive military and moral victory over its reviled neighbour, continues to inspire films and shows.

The Netflix limited series Operation Safed Sagar recounts the vital contributions of the Indian Air Force’s Golden Arrows Squadron. The squadron comprises young fighter pilots raring to go but not equipped to do so. Their commanding officer Tony Dhanoa (Jimmy Shergil) brings in Ajay Ahuja (Siddharth) to coach the youngsters.

item.title: Centre opposes plea in Supreme Court for income-based sub-quota within SC, ST and OBC reservations
item.description: The government maintained that reservations in government jobs and education are based on historical and social backwardness, not just economic status.
item.content:encoded:
The Union government on Thursday opposed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking directions for income-based prioritisation within reservations for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and the Other Backward Classes, Live Law reported.

The government maintained that the quotas are based on historical and social backwardness, not just on economic status.

Responding to the plea, the Centre stated that framing a policy on reservations in government jobs and educational institutes was within the executive’s domain, and not that of the courts.

The petitioners had sought directions from the court to the government to introduce sub-classification within the reservation matrix so that economically weaker persons in each quota category get priority.

The government said that the Constitution does not allow for changes to be made to reservations merely on economic criteria. Only Parliament can make changes to the quota lists based on historical, social and educational backwardness, Live Law quoted the government as having stated.

“These criteria are not spelt out in the Constitution but have become well established,” The Indian Express quoted the government as having stated.

It added that the creamy layer principle is not applicable in the context of reservations for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

item.description: The Congress leader alleged that the administration has been trying ‘every possible way’ to restrict him from speaking to students about exam irregularities.
item.content:encoded:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday said that the Bharatiya Janata Party government cannot stop him from raising the voice of students no matter how hard it tries.

Gandhi’s statement came after the management of a college in Uttar Pradesh’s Prayagraj revoked permission for an event where he was scheduled to speak with students about paper leaks and exam irregularities.

item.title: An evolutionary model that predates Darwin’s natural selection is making a comeback
item.description: Lamarckism contended that an organism may acquire characteristics in response to its environment and pass these on.
item.content:encoded:
Evolution is a fact of life. So much so that even the theory of evolution is evolving. Lately, a centuries-old discredited idea has been making a strong comeback. It helps us explain scientific observations that according to standard evolutionary theory should be impossible.

I’m referring to Lamarckism, named after theoretical proposals from French biologist Jean-Baptiste Lamarck in 1809. Lamarckism stands for the hypothesis that parents of a given organism may acquire or improve certain characteristics during their lifetimes in response to the demands of their environment. And they then somehow transmit those characteristics to their offspring, making those better able to cope with the same demands too.

Lamarck sought to explain why organisms and their environments fit so well together, and how organisms change over time, as observed in the fossil record. Of course, an alternative explanation was provided by Charles Darwin (and others) half a century later. Darwin’s ideas were built around natural selection, which says that some individuals within a species are born with differences that lead them to perform better and therefore reproduce more than others.

The article gave special status to the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir. While abrogating it, the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Union government had also bifurcated the state into two Union Territories: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

item.title: How the BJP stole the month of Sawan
item.description: In India’s Hindutva calendar, there is now only the ‘holy’, ‘sacred’ or ‘auspicious’ month of Shravan.
item.content:encoded:
There was a time when we called the monsoon month of Sawan by its name. In traditional lore, with its arrival, swings would appear in orchards. The air would be filled with the melodies of the kajri folk form and Raag Malhar. The Earth changed its attire as nature draped herself in a green veil.

Sawan meant relief and hope.

For farmers, Sawan is still Sawan. Even today, they call it by that name. Few other lives are bound to rain and drought as intimately as theirs. They await Sawan with particular longing. They know that the rhythm of cultivation changes with it.

Farmers know what the month means for paddy, maize, jowar, chana, black gram, cotton and other crops. Many of their festivals, too, fall in this month. There is Teej. There is Nag Panchami. The agricultural calendar and the Hindu ritual calendar have long lived together.

But we no longer inhabit that older sense of time. We now live within an official Hindutva calendar. It is no longer Sawan that begins but the auspicious month of Shravan. Every mention of Shravan must now be preceded by adjectives such as “holy, sacred or auspicious”.

item.title: Misinformation about health and wellness can be convincing – here is how to spot it
item.description: Claims spread through trusted social networks when people share it because they want to help or warn others.
item.content:encoded:
Recent reports have highlighted AI-generated “doctors” spreading dubious health advice to millions of social media users. Fabricated wellness trends can travel just as quickly. A supposed “pink jelly” weight-loss treatment, for example, reportedly fooled at least one celebrity.

These examples gain credibility in different ways. Influencers can appear familiar and sincere, while AI-generated doctors can look like qualified professionals. Neither familiarity nor the appearance of expertise tells us whether a medical claim is accurate.

Turning to friends and family for health advice is understandable. They may know our circumstances in ways that a healthcare professional cannot during a brief appointment. They can provide emotional support and practical help, and their advice is usually well meant. But somebody can care about us, speak honestly and still be wrong.

Truth and trust

My own research and wider research on digital health misinformation shows that trust can play an important part in deciding which claims people accept. Trust in clinicians and scientific institutions is generally associated with lower susceptibility to false health claims. Misinformation can nevertheless spread through trusted social networks when people share it because they want to help or warn others.

The Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee on Wednesday kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%.

The committee had cut the repo rate by 25 basis points from 5.50% in December and kept it unchanged in February, April and June.

A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point. Basis points are used to describe the percentage change in the value of a financial instrument.

Central banks usually reduce repo rates to stimulate economic growth by making borrowing cheaper for individuals and businesses. This translates to lower equated monthly instalments for borrowers.

item.title: When you hit ‘delete’, what really happens to your data?
item.description: There is a pressing need for provision of concise, accessible and clear information about how deletion really works.
item.content:encoded:
Deletion is a common part of modern life. We send files and folders to the recycle bin all the time, and often get rid of unwanted personal accounts. But do you know what really happens when you hit the “delete” button?

The process of deletion is often poorly explained by tech providers. Lack of transparency around how requests are processed, and the absence of clear confirmation that data has been removed, are frequently highlighted in research.

These issues are not limited to operating systems. On social media platforms and a wide range of subscription services, deletion mechanisms are often just as unclear. Such misconceptions can have serious implications for the wellbeing of users, exposing them to security and privacy vulnerabilities.

A further complication is that many users fear losing data, files, photos and videos through accidental deletion – a condition dubbed “diagraphephobia”. Though this is not a recognised pathology, studies of digital hoarding behaviour show that some people get very anxious at the thought of losing or accidentally deleting personal information such as photos and music.

Such concerns extend the amount of personal data that sits untended but undeleted, ready for potential misappropriation.

The manufacturers had been using added flavours rather than relying on the maturation of base materials such as molasses or malt to develop the products’ taste and aroma, the ministry added.

item.title: Long considered sacred, the golden langur, found in western Assam, is now an endangered animal
item.description: An excerpt from ‘Mammals of India’, by AJT Johnsingh and PO Nameer.
item.content:encoded:
Being confined to the sal-dominated (Shorea robusta) tropical moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests in India, and the sub-tropical and temperate broad-leaved forests in the India – Bhutan landscape, the golden langur stands out as the most restricted colobine (leaf-eating primate) species in India. Although described by earlier naturalists such as RB Pemberton and CM Inglis and co-workers during the 19th century as “cream colored monkey” and “Sankosh cream langurs”, the credit for suggesting that it could be a new species goes to EP Gee, a British tea planter and conservationist living in Assam. It was formally described in 1956 by H Khajuria of the Zoological Survey of India and named Presbytis geei in honour of Gee.

The golden langur is a medium-sized primate. Males weigh 10-12 kg and females 9.5-10 kg. They are less sexually dimorphic than other colobines such as grey langurs (Semnopithecus spp). Based on phylogeny and biogeography, T Wangchuk, a Bhutanese biologist, opined that Trachypithecus geei and T pileatus (capped langurs) branched off from an ancestral Trachypithecus from South Asia. In addition, the Sankosh River and Pele La mountain system in central Bhutan isolated a population of capped langurs during a warming period in central Bhutan, and this population later specialised into the morphologically distinct golden langur.

item.title: Change in transgender law cannot cancel rights already given, Supreme Court tells Centre
item.description: The amendments to the 2019 Act give the government complete power to determine gender identity and invalidate transgender cards, the petitioners contended.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court on Monday verbally clarified to the Union government that the 2026 amendments to the Transgender Persons Protection of Rights Act will not retrospectively or by default invalidate transgender cards issued to members of the community under the previous legislation, The Hindu reported.

The amendments to the 2019 Act, cleared by Parliament in March, redefine who qualifies as a transgender person. They remove transgender persons’ right to a self-perceived gender identity. They also limit the scope of the law to those with certain biological or physiological characteristics, intersex variations, or specific socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta.

The law makes medical evaluation and certification mandatory for legal gender recognition. It underlines that the authority to permit such transitions is vested in medical professionals operating under a medical board.

On Monday, petitioners against the amendments, who include members of the transgender community and activists, contended that the amendments give the government complete power to determine gender identity, The Hindu reported. Transgender cards issued by the government cannot be invalidated as they are an essential identity document, the petitioners said.

Twenty-two children have died due to Chandipura Vesiculovirus infection in Gujarat since the first week of July, The Indian Express quoted the state’s Health Minister Praful Pansheriya as saying.

Seven patients who tested positive are undergoing treatment at various civil hospitals, while six others have recovered and been discharged.

In a statement issued on Monday, the health minister’s office said that Gujarat has registered 184 suspected Chandipura virus cases so far, the newspaper reported. Among them, 35 were confirmed as positive, while the test results of 11 suspected cases were pending as of August 3.

All those infected are below 15 years of age, The Hindu reported.

The virus, also known as the Chandipura Viral Encephalitis, is transmitted primarily by sandflies and mosquitoes, including the Aedes aegypti species that bite during the day and is also known to spread dengue. The infection can lead to encephalitis, or the inflammation of the active tissues of the brain.

Children under the age of 15 years are most susceptible to the virus. Symptoms include fever, vomiting, altered sensorium, convulsions, diarrhoea, neurological deficit and meningeal irritation.

Pansheriya said on Monday that children admitted to hospitals at Gandhinagar, Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are being given specialised treatment, The Hindu reported.

Ceaușescu was very particular about how he looked on photographs – a team made sure wrinkles were removed and any photo looked perfectly staged. The widely circulated large posters of him had him in his 40s, people in Romania marveled at how his official posters refused to age. Like an unfortunate analogy for South Indian movie stardom, the crowd waving posters of the yesteryear blockbuster, facing an arthritic live version.

item.title: Justice MS Liberhan, who headed commission to probe Babri Masjid demolition, dies
item.description: He retired as the chief justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court on November 10, 2000, but continued to serve as the head of the Liberhan Commission.
item.content:encoded:
Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who headed a one-man judicial commission to investigate the circumstances that led to the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, died at the age of 87 on Sunday, The Hindu reported.

His last rites were performed on Monday.

Born on November 11, 1938, in a village near Chandigarh, Liberhan was a former Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh and Madras High Courts.

He began his career at the Punjab and Haryana High Court in 1964.

On February 11, 1987, Liberhan was elevated as a judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

He retired as the chief justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court on November 10, 2000, but continued to serve as the head of the Liberhan Commission.

The commission was set up days after the Babri Masjid was demolished on December 6, 1992 by Hindutva extremists who believed that the site was the birthplace of the deity Ram. It submitted its report to the Union government after 17 years, in 2009.

It went on to become one of the longest-running commissions of inquiry in India’s history.

The panel indicted Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh members for their alleged involvement in destroying the mosque. It also named several senior leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party such as Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani, Kalyan Singh, Pramod Mahajan and others.
